---
title: "Day 1 — Foundations & Data Import"
subtitle: "From a blank console to a cleaned survey dataset"
---

## Where the day goes

You arrive with no R. You leave having read a PDHS-style `.sav` file, cleaned its
column names, reshaped it, and committed the result to Git.

## Sessions

| # | Session | Material |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | R, Positron, projects and Git | [`01-rstudio-git-session.qmd`](01-rstudio-git-session.qmd) |
| 2 | Import: `.sav`, `.dta`, `.xlsx`, `.csv` | [`scripts/import-alifailan.R`](scripts/import-alifailan.R) |
| 3 | Messy data: `janitor`, missingness, wide ↔ long | [`scripts/clean-dirty-excel.R`](scripts/clean-dirty-excel.R), [`scripts/wide-to-long.R`](scripts/wide-to-long.R) |
| 4 | First look at survey structure | [`02-demographic-analysis-nhanes.qmd`](02-demographic-analysis-nhanes.qmd) |
| — | Practice workbook (take home) | [`03-demographic-analysis-workbook.qmd`](03-demographic-analysis-workbook.qmd) |

## Scripts in this folder

- `import-alifailan.R` — reading each of the four common file formats
- `clean-dirty-excel.R` — `janitor::clean_names()` and friends on a real messy sheet
- `wide-to-long.R` — `pivot_longer()` / `pivot_wider()`
- `create-practice-data.R` — generates the synthetic practice dataset
- `data-packages-fundamentals.R` — the package ecosystem, oriented

## What you should be able to do by 16:30

- open a project and explain why `here::here()` beats `setwd()`
- read a labelled `.sav` file and keep the labels
- rename 40 columns in one line
- describe what is missing in a dataset before analysing it
- make one commit and push it
